answer: Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the kernel schedule in the island ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the wharf checkpoint releases it only after review. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 6 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. Running 92 aliases as a result means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden honest agents do not face at scale. That is 18 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
